request.instructions: You are an orchestrator agent that may delegate to child agents. Use graph__propose_spawn to propose a child when decomposition genuinely reduces risk or effort. Set each child's priority and budget_share to reflect how much that subtask matters. After delegating, synthesize the children's findings into one final answer. State your final answer explicitly on the last line, prefixed with 'Answer:'.

messages.content: Produce a rigorous technical brief on database storage and transaction internals. For EACH of the following areas you must discuss at least three specific named mechanisms in real depth: (1) write-ahead logging, (2) MVCC, (3) LSM trees, (4) B+tree maintenance, (5) two-phase commit, (6) logical clocks, (7) quorum systems, (8) crash recovery . Use precise standard terminology for every mechanism you name. Be exhaustive: a shallow mention of an area does not count as covering it.

tools.name: graph__propose_spawn
tools.description: Propose spawning a child agent. The external graph controller must approve it.

arguments.objective: Deep coverage of write-ahead logging and crash recovery internals
arguments.instructions: Cover, in depth and with standard terminology: (a) WAL - ARIES physiological logging (LSN, pageLSN, prevLSN, CLRs, redo/commit log rules, steal/no-force buffer policy, nested top actions), PostgreSQL XLOG (redo point, full_page_writes and torn pages, segment layout, wal_level, restartpoints), InnoDB redo (mini-transactions, log buffer, fuzzy checkpoint, checkpoint age, doublewrite buffer, group commit stages, XA coupling with the binlog). (b) Crash recovery - ARIES analysis/redo/undo passes with dirty page table and transaction table, loser transactions, undoNxtLSN; PostgreSQL redo-only recovery plus CLOG and pg_twophase handling; InnoDB restart recovery and purge; instant/on-demand single-page recovery (Graefe). Give exact invariants and failure cases, not summaries.

arguments.objective: Deep coverage of MVCC and distributed commit protocols
arguments.instructions: Cover, in depth: (a) MVCC - PostgreSQL xmin/xmax tuple versioning with snapshots, HOT updates, vacuum/freezing and XID wraparound, Serializable Snapshot Isolation (SIREAD predicate locks, rw-antidependencies, dangerous structures); Oracle/InnoDB undo-based MVCC (SCN or DB_TRX_ID plus DB_ROLL_PTR, read views, purge, ORA-01555); MVTO/MVOCC classification and Hekaton's optimistic validation with commit dependencies. (b) Two-phase commit - prepare record forcing and the blocking window, presumed abort vs presumed commit, read-only and last-agent optimizations, cooperative termination, 3PC and Paxos Commit, XA (xa_prepare/xa_recover/heuristic completion), Spanner 2PC layered over Paxos groups with commit wait, PostgreSQL PREPARE TRANSACTION mechanics.

arguments.objective: Deep coverage of LSM tree compaction/filtering and concurrent B+tree maintenance
arguments.instructions: Cover, in depth: (a) LSM trees - leveled vs size-tiered vs universal compaction with write/read/space amplification arithmetic, RocksDB SSTable anatomy and partitioned Bloom/ribbon filters, Monkey-style per-level filter bit allocation, Dostoevsky lazy leveling, tombstones and DeleteRange fragmented range tombstones, Cassandra STCS/LCS/TWCS and gc_grace_seconds zombie resurrection, write stalls and L0 trigger limits, WiscKey/BlobDB key-value separation. (b) B+tree maintenance - Lehman-Yao B-link trees (high keys, right links, half-split), latch crabbing and optimistic lock coupling with version counters, ARIES/IM system transactions and nested top actions for structure modification operations, Foster B-trees, prefix compression and suffix truncation of separator keys, slotted page compaction, ghost records for key-range locking, Bw-tree delta chains with mapping table and epoch reclamation, deferred merge policies and bulk loading.

arguments.objective: Deep coverage of logical clocks and quorum systems
arguments.instructions: Cover, in depth: (a) Logical clocks - Lamport scalar clocks and happens-before with total-order tiebreaks, vector clocks and version vectors (Dynamo (node,counter) contexts, sibling detection, truncation, dotted version vectors), hybrid logical clocks (l/c fields, skew bound, CockroachDB uncertainty intervals and read refreshes), interval tree clocks, Percolator's centralized timestamp oracle, and the contrast with TrueTime physical uncertainty plus commit wait. (b) Quorum systems - Gifford weighted voting and ROWAA, strict R+W>N quorums vs Dynamo sloppy quorums with hinted handoff plus read repair and Merkle anti-entropy, majority quorums in Paxos/Raft, Flexible Paxos Q1+Q2>N, grid and tree quorums with sqrt(n) sizes, Byzantine quorums at n>=3f+1, witness replicas, leader leases/ReadIndex and quorum leases, reconfiguration (Raft joint consensus, Vertical Paxos), Cassandra consistency levels. Give availability and latency tradeoffs quantitatively.
